newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's 1998 budget may rise up to 10 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: Peru's 1998 budget may rise up to 10 pct - paper.

text.p: Peru's 1998 spending budget may be up to 10 percent higher than the 24.77 billion sol program approved for 1997, Congress' new budget commission head Carlos Lam said in an interview published Monday.
"According to the first signs that we have, it is possible there will be an increase, but this will not be large. I estimate that it should not be above 10 percent," he told financial daily Gestion.

Lam added the government would need Congress to approve a four billion sol supplementary credit to cover total 1997 spending. "This is basically due to the outflow from the debt agreement with the foreign banks, and the emergency programs," he said.

He was referring to Peru's recently-closed Brady Plan to restructure foreign commercial debt, and a special fund to cope with the effects of the destructive El Nino weather phenomenon forming off the Pacific coast.
Congress' commission works closely with the government in the preparation of spending plans, and the full legislature usually passes the cabinet's proposals without significant changes.
